subject: ela
intro: In a good group discussion, you come prepared, follow the rules (take turns, listen), ask questions, and build on what others say. Building on an idea means adding to it or connecting your point to someone else's. Third graders take part in discussions the right way.

items.prompt: Your group is discussing a book. Before the meeting, what should you do to come prepared?

steps: Coming prepared means getting ready ahead of time.
You should read the book and think of ideas.
So you read the book and bring ideas to share.
solution.answer: Read the book and bring ideas.

items.prompt: A classmate says, 'The hero was brave.' You add, 'Yes, and she was also kind when she helped the old man.' What are you doing?

steps: You agreed and added a new point to theirs.
That is building on their idea.
So you are building on the idea.

items.prompt: What should you do when you do not understand what a classmate said?

steps: You can ask a question to understand.
So you ask a question for help.

items.prompt: Coming to a discussion ready is being ____.
Adding to a classmate's point is ____ on their idea.
When it is not your turn, you should ____.
